questions.question: Which of the following diseases is a potential contender for worldwide eradication?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Polio.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __ Key Points__

__
 
• **Polio** is a potential contender for **worldwide eradication** because it is a **vaccine-preventable disease** and there are effective vaccines available.
 
• The **World Health Organization **(WHO) has been leading the global effort to **eradicate polio **since **1988,** and significant progress has been made in reducing the number of cases worldwide.
 
• **Tuberculosis, measles, and malaria** are not currently considered potential contenders for worldwide eradication because they are more difficult to **control and eliminate** due to various factors such as **drug resistance, lack of effective vaccines,** and **complex transmission patterns.**
 
• However, efforts are still being made to reduce the burden of these diseases through various strategies such as **improved diagnostics, treatment, and prevention measures.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuberculosis** is a** bacterial infection** that primarily affects the **lungs** but can also affect other parts of the body.

 
 
• It is a major cause of** illness** and **death** worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Measles** is a highly contagious** viral **infection.
 
 
• It can cause serious complications such as** pneumonia, brain damage, and death,** and it is still a major cause of death among young children in many parts of the world.
 
 
 
• **Malaria** is a parasitic infection that is transmitted by **mosquitoes**, and it can cause **fever, chills, and flu-like symptoms**, and in severe cases, it can lead to organ failure and death.
 
 
• It is a major public health problem in many **tropical and subtropical **regions of the world.

questions.question: Due to which of the following reasons can money be differentiated from other physical assets that can perform the function of store of value?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Money is easy to store.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Money **can be differentiated from other **physical assets** that can perform the function of store of value due to the following reasons:
 
• **Easy to store**:
 
 
• Money can be stored in a variety of forms, including **cash, bank deposits, or digital wallets**.
 
• It does not require any **specialized storage** or maintenance.
 
• Other physical assets like** real estate or art **may require specialized storage **facilities and maintenance.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liquidity:** 

 
 
• Money is **highly liquid **and can be easily converted into cash without any loss in its value. 
 
• Other physical assets like **real estate or gold** may have a high store of value but may not be easily convertible into cash.
 
 
 
• **Common acceptability:** 
 
 
• Money is universally accepted and recognized as a** medium of exchange**. 
 
• It is accepted by all parties in a** transaction**, making it easier to conduct **trade and commerce.** 
 
• Other physical assets** may not** have the same level of acceptance.
 
 
 
• **Neutral:**
 
 
• Money is neutral and **does not **carry any emotional or personal attachment. 
 
• It is a standardized form of currency that is free from any **personal biases or opinions**.
 
• Other physical assets may have** sentimental value **attached to them.

questions.question: English as the official language of India for higher education was incorporated in the resolution formulation by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Macaulay.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Macaulay** was the one who **incorporated English** as the **official language** of India for higher education in the resolution formulation.
 
• He was the **President** of the **Committee of Public Instruction**, which was responsible for the formulation of the resolution.
 
• The resolution was passed in **1835** and it aimed to introduce **English education** in India.
 
• Lord Macaulay believed that the introduction of **English education **would create a class of Indians who would be "Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect.
 
• The resolution had far-reaching consequences and played a significant role in **shaping modern India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Hastings** was the **Governor-General of India** from **1813 to 1823.**

 
 
• He is known for his **policies of territorial expansion** and **consolidation.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Wellesley** was the Governor-General of India from **1798 to 1805.**
 
 
• He is known for his policies of** territorial expansion** and the **Subsidiary Alliance system.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie** was the Governor-General of India from **1848 to 1856.**
 
 
• He is known for his policies of **modernization and administrative reforms,** including the introduction of railways and telegraph lines.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT the reason why 'final' goods are called so?

options.text: They are meant for final use.
They are the last to be consumed.
They will not pass through any more stages of production.
They are not processed or transformed further:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are the last to be consumed.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __ Key Points__

__
 
• They are meant for** final use**.

 
 
• This is a **correct reason** why final goods are called so.
 
• Final goods are produced for **direct consumption **or use by the end-users.
 
 
 
• They are the** last to be consumed**.
 
 
• This is an** incorrect reason **why final goods are called so.
 
• The order of consumption **does not **determine whether a good is final or not.
 
 
 
• They will not pass through any more** stages of production**.
 
 
• This is a** correct reason** why final goods are called so.
 
• Final goods are ready for** use or sale** and do not require any further processing or transformation.
 
 
 
• They are not** processed or transformed** further.
 
 
• This is a** correct reason** why final goods are called so.
 
• Final goods are the **end products **of the production process and do not require any further processing or transformation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Final goods** are also known as **consumer goods** as they are meant for **direct consumption** by the end-users.
 
• They are the end products of the production process and are ready for **use or sale** in the market.
 
• Final goods are different from i**ntermediate goods,** which are used as raw materials or components in the production of final goods.

questions.question: The provision for the post of Vice-President in the Indian Constitution was taken from ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Indian Constitution** was heavily influenced by the Constitution of the** United States of America.**
 
• The post of Vice-President in India is similar to the post in the US, where the Vice-President is the** second-in-command** to the President.
 
• The Vice-President in India is also the **ex-officio Chairman **of the **Rajya Sabha, **the upper house of the Indian Parliament.
 
• The post of Vice-President was included in the Indian Constitution to ensure **continuity and stability** in the event of the** President's absence or death.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **France:**

 
 
• The French Constitution** does not** have a post of Vice-President.
 
• The French government has a **Prime Minister** who is the **head of government **and a **President** who is the **head of state.**
 
 
 
• **Ireland:**
 
 
• The Irish Constitution has a post of** Vice-President,** but it is known as the **"Tnaiste" **and is appointed by the Prime Minister.
 
• The Tnaiste is** not **the ex-officio Chairman of any house of parliament.
 
 
 
• **Japan:**
 
 
• The Japanese Constitution **does not** have a post of Vice-President.
 
• The Japanese government has a **Prime Minister** who is the head of government and an **Emperor** who is the **ceremonial head of state.**

questions.question: According to the Köppen classification, which letter code represents a tropical climate with a dry winter season found in large parts of peninsular India south of the Tropic of Cancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aw.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aw** represents a tropical climate with a** dry winter season **found in large parts of peninsular India south of the **Tropic of Cancer.**
 
• Climates are classified according to **Köppen's five primary groups**, with **seasonal precipitation** and** temperature** patterns serving as the basis for group divisions.
 
• A stands for** tropical,** B for **desert**, C for **temperate**, D for **continental,** and E for **polar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BWk **represents an arid climate with **cold winters and hot summers,** found in regions with **low precipitation** and** high evaporation rates.**
 
• **CWh** represents a **subtropical climate** with **dry winters and hot summers**, found in regions with **mild to moderate rainfall **and **high humidity.**
 
• **Dw** represents a severe continental climate with **dry winters and hot summers,** found in regions with** low precipitation** and** large temperature** fluctuations between seasons.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the characteristics of a crystalline solid?

options.text: There is no precise melting point
Changes abruptly from solid to liquid when heated

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Changes abruptly from solid to liquid when heated.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crystalline solids** have a** highly ordered **and **repeating atomic arrangement**, which gives them their **characteristic geometric shapes.**
 
• They have a precise **melting point,** which is the temperature at which the **ordered atomic arrangement** breaks down and the solid transitions to a liquid state.
 
• The **3-dimensional layout** of a crystalline solid is **highly regular and symmetrical,** with atoms or molecules arranged in a repeating pattern.
 
• When heated, a crystalline solid undergoes an abrupt phase transition from **solid to liquid**, without passing through an intermediate liquid crystal phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Crystalline solids are **resistant to geometric deformation** due to their highly ordered atomic arrangement.
 
• Crystalline solids have a **precise melting point, **which is a characteristic feature of their structure.
 
• The layout of a crystalline solid is highly **regular and symmetrical**, with no unevenness in the arrangement of atoms or molecules.
 
• The key term **'crystalline solid'** refers to a type of solid material with a **highly ordered atomic structure**, which gives it unique physical and chemical properties.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the number of atoms in one mole of CH₃ OH?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.6 × 1024.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CH₃OH** is the chemical formula for **methanol**, which is a **colorless liquid** with a **mild odor.**
 
• One mole of any substance contains **6.02 x 10²³ particles**, which is known as **Avogadro's number.**
 
• In CH₃OH, there are **6 atoms** in one molecule: 1 carbon, 4 hydrogen, and 1 oxygen.
 
• To calculate the number of atoms in one mole of CH₃OH, we **multiply Avogadro's number** by the** number of atoms** in one molecule, which is 6.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is 6.02 x 10²³ x 6 =** 3.6 x 10²⁴** atoms in one mole of CH₃OH.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Usually, the Avogadro constant is represented by **NA or L**.
 
• The quantity of substance in a sample, which is calculated by dividing the number of constituent particles by NA, uses it as a** normalizing factor.**
 
• Depending on the substance and the type of reaction, the units could be** molecules, atoms, ions, or electrons.**

questions.question: Rann Utsav is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rann Utsav** is a cultural festival that takes place in the **Rann of Kutch**, a vast **salt desert** in **Gujarat.**
 
• It usually happens between **November and February** and lasts for several days.
 
• The festival showcases the rich heritage and traditions of **Gujarat**, with a focus on **local art, music, dance, and cuisine.**
 
• Visitors can enjoy various activities such as **camel rides, folk performances, handicrafts shopping, and stargazing**.
 
• Rann Utsav is organized by the **Gujarat Tourism Department** and attracts a large number of domestic and international tourists every year.
 
• It is considered one of the biggest cultural events in India and helps promote** tourism and the local economy.**
 
• Some of the popular attractions during Rann Utsav include the **Tent City,** a temporary settlement of luxury tents and cottages, the **White Desert**, a mesmerizing landscape of salt crystals and mirages, and the** Kala Dungar,** the highest point in Kutch offering panoramic views of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goa** is a state in southwest India known for its **beaches, nightlife, and Portuguese colonial architecture.**

 
 
• It hosts several festivals throughout the year, such as the** Goa Carnival, the International Film Festival of India, and the Sunburn Music Festival.**
 
 
 
• **Punjab **is a state in northern India known for its **agriculture, cuisine, and religious diversity**.
 
 
• It celebrates several festivals related to **Sikhism**, such as the** Guru Nanak Jayanti, the Baisakhi, and the Holla Mohalla.**
 
 
 
• **Haryana **is a state in northern India known for its historical and cultural significance.
 
 
• It hosts several fairs and festivals, such as the **Surajkund Crafts Mela, the Pinjore Heritage Festival, and the Gita Jayanti.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic questions every society needs to answer?

options.text: How should the goods be distributed?
What goods and services to produce?
How should the goods be exchanged?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __How should the goods be exchanged?__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• "How should the goods be exchanged?" This is **not **one of the basic questions every society needs to answer because it is a **sub-question** of the distribution question.
 
• The other options are all basic questions that **every society needs** to answer in order to function properly.
 
• "How should goods be produced?" refers to the methods and technologies used to create** goods and services.**
 
• "What goods and services to produce?" refers to the decisions made about what** products and services** are necessary for society and how to allocate resources to produce them.
 
• "How should the goods be distributed?" refers to how the products and services are **divided and allocated** among the members of the society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The main keyword mentioned is **"basic questions."** 
 
• These are **fundamental questions** that every society needs to answer in order to **survive and thrive.**
 
• The basic questions of economics are often referred to as the **"Four Fundamental Questions of Economics."**
 
• These questions are: **What to produce? How to produce? For whom to produce?** and **How to distribute the goods and services.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Some of them available to legal expertise.
Some of them are available to foreigners.
The Constitution does not provide for their direct enforcement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Constitution does not provide for their direct enforcement.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental duties** are a set of moral obligations that are mentioned in the **Indian Constitution**, which every citizen is expected to follow.
 
• These duties are **not directly** enforceable by law, but they serve as a reminder to **citizens to be responsible** and **patriotic** towards their country.
 
• **Reasonable restrictions** can be imposed on these duties if they clash with other fundamental rights or public interests.
 
• None of these duties are available to **legal expertise or foreigners**, they are only applicable to Indian citizens.
 
• The concept of fundamental duties was added to the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment in 1976.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• List of **11 fundamental duties:**

 
 
• Respect the **national flag and anthem**, and abide by the constitution.
 
• Adhere to the **freedom struggle's** ideals.
 
• Preserve India's **integrity and sovereignty**.
 
• When called upon, **defend **the nation and perform national duties.
 
• Fostering a sense of **shared fraternity.**
 
• Preserve the nation's **diverse culture.**
 
• Keep the surroundings** natural.**
 
• Develop a** kind and scientific temperament.**
 
• Keep** public property safe** and abstain from **violence.**
 
• Aim for **greatness** in every aspect of your life.
 
• It is the responsibility of all parents and guardians to send their children, aged** 6 to 14, to school. **

questions.question: Identify the true statement among the following.

options.text: Income Tax is an Indirect Tax
Goods and Services Tax is a direct tax
Fees and Fines collected is a non-tax receipt
Borrowings from the public is a revenue receipt

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fees and Fines collected is a non-tax receipts.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fees and fines** collected are considered **non-tax receipts** because they are **not imposed **as a result of any legislative power or authority.
 
• The government's recurring income from sources **other than taxes** is known as** non-tax revenue.**
 
• These are the taxes collected that do not originate from **levies **on the general populace.
 
• Payments received that** do not** give rise to** liabilities or a claim **against the government are known as revenue receipts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income tax** is a tax levied on the income earned by an individual or entity.

 
 
• It is a **direct tax **as it is levied on the** income of the taxpayer.**
 
 
 
• **Goods and Services Tax** (GST) is a tax imposed on the **supply of goods and services.**
 
 
• It is an **indirect tax** as it is** not levied directly **on the income of the taxpayer.
 
 
 
• **Borrowings** from the public are a form of **external debt**.
 
 
• The government borrows from the **public to finance** its developmental activities.
 
• It is a **capital receipt **as it** does not **generate regular income for the government.

questions.question: Which of the following is a folk dance from the state of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tippani.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tippani** is a **folk dance** from the state of **Gujarat.**
 
• It involves a group of women dancing in a** circle** and clapping their hands in** rhythm. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a tribal dance form that is performed during various occasions such as** weddings, festivals, and harvest season.**
 
 
 
• **Dhamal** is a folk dance form in Haryana whose origin is rooted back to the days of the Mahabharat.
 
 
• The Dhamal dance is famous in the Gurgaon area,
 
• It is performed by both **Hindus and Muslims** and involves singing and dancing in a circle.

questions.question: The Jog Falls, one of the highest waterfalls in India is the cataract of which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sharavati.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jog Falls** is located in the state of** Karnataka**, India, and is formed by the **Sharavati River.**
 
• The Sharavati River originates in the** Western Ghats** and flows towards the **west coast of India **before merging with the **Arabian Sea.**
 
• Jog Falls is also known as **Gerosoppa Falls** and is one of the most popular tourist destinations in** Karnataka.**
 
• The height of the falls is around **830 feet** and it is divided into four distinct segments - **Raja, Rani, Roarer, and Rocket.**
 
• The waterfall is at its peak during the monsoon season, which is between **June and September.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada** is a river that flows through **central India**.

 
 
• It is known for its **marble rocks and the Narmada Dam.**
 
 
 
• **Tungabhadra** is a river that flows through the states of **Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh**.
 
 
• It is known for the **Tungabhadra Dam **and the **Hampi World Heritage site.**
 
 
 
• **Cauvery** is a river that flows through the states of **Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.**
 
 
• It is known for its delta region and the **Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary.**

questions.question: Narayan Guru, a social reformer from Ezhava caste and who propagated an anti-caste movement, was born in which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narayan Guru** was a **social reformer, philosopher, and spiritual leader **who lived from **1856 to 1928.**
 
• He was born in **Chempazhanthy, **a village near **Thiruvananthapuram **in Kerala.
 
• Narayan Guru was a strong advocate for **social equality** and worked to end the **caste system** in India.
 
• He founded the **Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana** (SNDP) Yogam, which was a social organization that aimed to uplift the **Ezhava community** and other marginalized groups in Kerala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kerala's Ezhavas **belong to the **Bahujan caste.** 
 
• The Ezhava used to work as **laborers in agriculture, small-scale farmers, toddy tappers**, and **liquor merchants**.
 
• Some of them were also **weavers, **and some of them were **Ayurvedic practitioners.**
